record.paper_title: Trimer Covers in the Triangular Grid: Twenty Mostly Open Problems
record.original_question: Let T113(a,b) count tilings of the (a,b)-benzel when both stone orientations are allowed and all three bone orientations are allowed. Is the sequence T113(n, 2n-3), defined for n >= 4, 2-adically continuous as a function of n?

evidence.quote: For 0 <= i, j <= 1 and 0 <= k <= 3 we define Tijk (a, b) as the number of ways to tile the (a, b)-benzel if the set of allowed prototiles contains the right stone iff i = 1, contains the left stone iff j = 1, and contains k of the bones. We say that such a tiling is an i, j, k tiling.
Problem 16: Is T113 (n, 2n - 3) 2-adically continuous as a function of n >= 4?
The sequence appears to be constant mod 2, constant mod 4, 2-periodic mod 8, and 8-periodic mod 16.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the triangular grid in the plane. For integers a, b with appropriate parity, the (a,b)-benzel is a specific hexagonally-symmetric region of the triangular grid (the natural analog of the Aztec diamond for the triangular lattice). Consider tilings of the (a,b)-benzel using prototiles drawn from a fixed set. The prototiles are of two types: "stones" (each stone is a certain rhombus-shaped tile coming in two chiral orientations, called the right stone and the left stone) and "bones" (each bone is a tribone-shaped tile coming in three rotational orientations). For i,j in {0,1} and k in {0,1,2,3}, define T_{ijk}(a,b) to be the number of tilings of the (a,b)-benzel using prototiles from the set that contains the right stone iff i=1, contains the left stone iff j=1, and contains exactly k of the three bones (for a specified choice of which k bones, taken to be canonical).

In particular, T_{113}(a,b) counts tilings of the (a,b)-benzel where both stones and all three bones are allowed.

A sequence (c_n) of integers (n ≥ n_0) is said to be 2-adically continuous as a function of n if for every positive integer N there exists a positive integer M such that whenever n ≡ n' (mod 2^M), one has c_n ≡ c_{n'} (mod 2^N); equivalently, the map n ↦ c_n extends to a continuous function from the 2-adic integers Z_2 to itself.

Question: Is the sequence T_{113}(n, 2n-3), defined for n ≥ 4, 2-adically continuous as a function of n?
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as one of twenty mostly open problems about trimer covers/benzel tilings on the triangular grid. Empirical data show the sequence appears constant mod 2, constant mod 4, 2-periodic mod 8, and 8-periodic mod 16, but no proof of 2-adic continuity is reported. No subsequent resolution was located in available sources.

status_evidence.title: Jim Propp's Benzel Tilings Site
status_evidence.snippet: Resource page on benzel tilings, listing open problems and progress related to trimer covers and (a,b)-benzels.
status_evidence.claim: Benzel tilings problems are tracked on Propp's project page; no resolution of the 2-adic continuity question for T113(n,2n-3) is reported.

status_evidence.title: A Pentagonal Number Theorem for Tribone Tilings
status_evidence.snippet: Paper on tribone tilings of benzels, part of the body of work to which the open problem belongs.
status_evidence.claim: Related literature addresses tribone tilings of benzels but does not resolve the 2-adic continuity of T113(n,2n-3).
